claim_text: A Pi extension is a TypeScript module that subscribes to lifecycle events, registers LLM-callable custom tools, and adds commands.
evidence_span: Extensions are TypeScript modules that extend pi's behavior. They can subscribe to lifecycle events, register custom tools callable by the LLM, add commands, and more.

claim_text: Pi extensions run with the user's full system permissions and can execute arbitrary code, so only trusted sources should be installed.
evidence_span: Extensions run with your full system permissions and can execute arbitrary code. Only install from sources you trust.

claim_text: Only extensions placed in Pi's auto-discovered locations can be hot-reloaded with /reload; a -e path is for quick tests.
evidence_span: Extensions in auto-discovered locations can be hot-reloaded with `/reload`.

claim_text: A Pi extension's tool_call handler can block a tool call by returning block with an optional reason and terminate flag, and can patch arguments by mutating event.input in place.
evidence_span: Return values from `tool_call` control blocking via `{ block: true, reason?: string, terminate?: boolean }`

claim_text: A Pi extension factory may run in an invocation that never starts a session, so background resources — processes, sockets, watchers, timers — must be deferred to session_start or the handler that needs them.
evidence_span: Extension factories may run in invocations that never start a session. Do not start background resources such as processes, sockets, file watchers, or timers from the factory.

claim_text: The first user/global or CLI Pi extension whose project_trust handler answers yes or no owns the trust decision and suppresses the built-in prompt; undecided passes it on.
evidence_span: A user/global or CLI extension that returns `"yes"` or `"no"` owns the decision; the first yes/no decision wins and suppresses the built-in trust prompt.

claim_text: Pi accepts registerTool calls after startup as well as at load, refreshing the new tool into the same session so the LLM can call it without a /reload.
evidence_span: `pi.registerTool()` works both during extension load and after startup. You can call it inside `session_start`, command handlers, or other event handlers. New tools are refreshed immediately in the same session, so they appear in `pi.getAllTools()` and are callable by the LLM without `/reload`.

claim_text: Pi appends a custom tool's promptGuidelines bullets flat into the shared Guidelines section with no tool-name prefix, so each bullet must name its own tool rather than say "this tool".
evidence_span: `promptGuidelines` bullets are appended flat to the `Guidelines` section with no tool name prefix. Each guideline must name the tool it refers to — avoid "Use this tool when..." because the LLM cannot tell which tool "this" means.
